1143-panama-field-study-semester: With the Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute. See p. 1286.
1143-mcgill-east-africa-field-study-seme: 15 credits, interdisciplinary, coordinated by Geography. See p. 1286.
1143-barbados-field-study-semester: 15 credits at the Bellairs Research Institute, September to December, on global issues and sustainability in the Caribbean. See p. 1286.
1144-program-description: With any Science primary program outside Biology; 6 credits may overlap. See the adviser early: Nancy Nelson, Stewart Biology Building.
1144-complementary-courses-10-credits: 9–10 credits, including the listed course, plus two Biology courses at 300+. If you've done CHEM 212, choose another with the Adviser's approval.
1144-program-description-2: Flexible fundamentals, from molecules to ecosystems, including development, behaviour and evolution, for varied interests. 45–47 credits.
1144-core-6-8-credits: 3–4 and 3–4 from two lists. If you've done CHEM 212, take Organic Chemistry 2 or an approved Biology course.
1145-other-15-credits: Biology at 300–500, at least 3 at 400–500. Up to 6 of other science with permission, and up to 6 of research.
1145-program-description: Molecules to ecosystems, with focus on molecular, cellular and developmental biology; conservation, ecology and evolution; or neurobiology and behaviour.
1145-core-12-13-credits: 3–4 from CHEM (if you've done CHEM 212, Organic Chemistry 2 or an approved Biology course), and 3 each from Blocks A, B and C.
1146-other-15-credits: Biology at 300–500, 6 at 400–500. Up to 6 of research and up to 6 of other science with approval.
1146-program-description: For those wanting physical science applied to biology, with ecology and evolutionary, or physical biology, streams, mixing theory and experiment. 68–73 credits, depending on MATH 222 and CHEM 212.
1146-advising-notes-for-u0-students: Choose Foundation courses with the Adviser. Recommended for U1 students with CGPA 3.20 or CEGEP entrants with a Math/Science R-score of 28.0.
1146-bio-physical-sciences-core-31-credi: With CHEM 212 or MATH 222 equivalents, take a 3–4 credit complementary with a stream adviser. If you can program, take COMP 250 instead of COMP 202.
1147-quantitative-biology-theoretical-ec: 9 credits, with lists of recommendations by stream. COMP 350 or MATH 317. COMP 251 requires MATH 235 or 240.
1148-program-description: Mathematical biology, with Applied Mathematics and Statistics streams, and Ecology and Evolutionary Biology, Molecular Evolution, and Neurosciences streams.
1148-degree-requirements-b-sc: Meet program and degree requirements (p. 1106); see SOUSA's Degree Planning Guide. Choose Foundation courses with the Advisor. Recommended for U1 CGPA 3.2 or CEGEP R-score 28.0.
1148-bio-physical-sciences-core: With CHEM 212 or MATH 222 equivalents, take electives. COMP 202 or 204, or COMP 250 if you can program. MATH 223 or 247.
1148-complementary-courses-39-credits: 21 of BIOL, NEUR, PHGY or PSYC, including a stream, and 18 of MATH.
1148-math-or-biology-research-course: 3–6 credits, counted toward the BIOL or MATH total. At least 6 of the remainder at 400+.
1149-math-courses: 15 credits if MATH 410 was your research course, otherwise 18, from Stream 1 or 2 and Remaining Math.
1149-remaining-math-courses: 3–9 from either sequence or the list.
1149-biol-neur-phgy-phys-psyc-courses: 18 credits with a 3-credit BIOL research course, or 15 with a 6-credit one, including a stream. Some have prerequisites.
1149-ecology-and-evolutionary-biology-st: 15–21 credits: 3 from one course, 3 of field courses (others with permission), and 9–15 from the list. BIOL 202 or 302.
1150-remaining-biol-neur-phgy-psyc: Top up to 18–21 from the streams; others with the Advisor's approval.
1150-program-description: Concentrated research in molecular, cellular and developmental biology; conservation, ecology and evolution; or neurobiology and behaviour. Enter at the end of U2 with CGPA 3.50 and an approved 9- or 12-credit proposal (BIOL 479D1/D2 or 480D1/D2). Graduate with 3.50; First Class at 3.75.
1151-other-12-15-credits: 15 with BIOL 479D1/D2, or 12 with 480D1/D2, at 300–500, 6 at 400–500. Up to 6 from other sciences with permission, and up to 3 of past research.
1151-program-description: Physical science applied to biology through courses and a research project, in theoretical ecology and evolution, or physical biology. CGPA 3.50 to enter and finish; First Class at 3.75. 74–79 credits, depending on MATH 222 and CHEM 212.
1151-bio-physical-sciences-core-31-credi: With CHEM 212 or MATH 222 equivalents, take complementaries with a stream adviser. COMP 250 instead of COMP 202 if you can program. One each of MATH 223 or 247, 315 or 325, 323 or 356, 324 or 357. 6 credits of MATH or PHYS must be at honours level; all 500-level MATH count.
1152-stream-2-physical-biology: 21 credits: 9 from the first list (BIOL 319 or PHYS 319), 6 at 300-level and 6 at 500-level.
1153-complementary-courses-9-credits: Recommendations by stream. COMP 350 or MATH 317. COMP 251 requires MATH 235 or 240.
1154-about-biotechnology: Using organisms and gene products for commercial and medical ends, which needs biology and engineering plus depth in a subject like molecular genetics. The Minor, from Engineering and Science, joins your main program.
Tell your advisor and the program's advisor, and declare by U2 registration. Before registering, the supervisor certifies your course list. Check prerequisites. BIOT 505 counts as Science.
1154-general-regulations: 24 credits, 18 exclusively for the Minor and outside your primary program. C or better.
1154-biotechnology-biot-minor-program: Supervisor: Audrey Moores, Maass Chemistry Building, 801 Sherbrooke St. W. Advisor: Chantal Grignon, Life Sciences Building, 3649 Sir William Osler.
1154-program-description: 24 credits, 18 exclusively for the Minor. Substitute approved courses for any required ones in your main program.
1154-complementary-courses-9-credits: From outside your main department: three from one list, or three others with approval.
1156-program-description: For Chemistry students, on process engineering and linking molecular science to industry. It doesn't qualify you as a licensed engineer.
1157-complementary-courses-6-credits: Any undergraduate Chemical Engineering courses except CHEE 456, 494, 495 and 496.
1157-pre-program-prerequisites: From Foundation: CHEM 110, 120, BIOL 112, MATH 133, MATH 140/141 or 150/151, and PHYS 101/102 or 131/142, or equivalents. Quebec students: a suitable DEC. MATH 150 and 151 replace MATH 222.
1157-required-basic-core-courses-43-cred: Not certified by the Ordre des chimistes du Québec; to work as a chemist in Quebec, take another B.Sc. Chemistry. COMP 202 or 208 and MATH 222 are strongly recommended in U1. CEGEP-equivalent courses are skipped; others see the Adviser.
1158-pre-program-prerequisites: From Foundation: the listed course, MATH 150/151, PHYS 101/102 or 131/142, or equivalents. Quebec students: a suitable DEC. MATH 150 and 151 replace MATH 222.
1158-required-courses-53-credits: COMP 202 or 208 and MATH 222 are strongly recommended in U1. CEGEP-equivalent courses are skipped, but Chemistry ones must be replaced in that discipline for Ordre des chimistes eligibility. Others see the Adviser.
1159-complementary-courses-6-credits: 6 of CHEM at 400+, or MATH 315 and 3 of CHEM at 400+.
1159-required-courses-57-credits: COMP 202 or 208 and MATH 222 are strongly recommended in U1. CEGEP-equivalent courses are skipped, but Chemistry ones must be replaced for Ordre des chimistes eligibility. MATH 150 and 151 replace MATH 222.
1160-program-description: Chemistry fundamentals with physical, computational and math skills for biophysical research in biomedicine and biotech. 65 or 66 credits.
1160-required-courses-59-credits: MATH 222 and 315 are strongly recommended in U1.
1160-bio-physical-sciences-core: CEGEP-equivalent courses are skipped. Ordre des chimistes eligibility needs extra chemistry electives. Not currently accredited by the Canadian Society for Chemistry. MATH 150 and 151 replace MATH 222.
1160-chemistry: CEGEP-equivalent courses are skipped. Ordre des chimistes eligibility needs extra chemistry electives. Not currently accredited by the Canadian Society for Chemistry.
